entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.description: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.summary: EMA issued guidance clarifying the PIP compliance verification procedure and paediatric reward details.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must ensure their PIP submissions meet verification criteria and understand the paediatric reward eligibility and reporting requirements.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice of Compliance (NOC) Data Extracts
entries.description: The data extract is a series of compressed ASCII text files of the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.summary: The Notice of Compliance database is now available as a series of compressed ASCII text files.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams can access up-to-date NOC information for regulatory submissions and monitoring.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
entries.description: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027…
entries.summary: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot becomes a permanent initiative from January 2027.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams will need to plan for ongoing, continuous guidance on preparing clinical trial applications and adjust timelines accordingly.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Product monograph brand safety updates
entries.description: Product monograph brand safety updates for Submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026
entries.summary: Brand safety information has been added to product monographs for submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must incorporate these updates into their documentation to ensure compliance and accurate product labeling.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0120)
entries.description: This document is intended to help market authorization holders comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: New guidance on reporting drug shortages and discontinuations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must now report shortages/discontinuations per sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada (GUI-0145)
entries.description: This document is intended to help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new guideline clarifies how drug establishment licence holders must distribute drugs intended for the Canadian market but for use outside Canada.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams responsible for export of Canadian-market drugs must review and implement these distribution requirements to remain compliant with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on the exceptional importation and sale of drugs in response to shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0148)
entries.description: This document will help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: The guide provides new procedures for drug establishments to import and sell drugs to address shortages and discontinuations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must ensure their operations comply with the updated importation and sale rules to avoid penalties and support patient access.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs in response to drug shortages (GUI-0500)
entries.description: This document will help market authorization holders and drug establishment licence holders understand how to comply with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: Provides guidance on how to extend expiration dates of marketed drugs to address shortages.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review C.010.014 to C.10.021 to ensure compliance when extending expiry dates.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Register of Innovative Drugs
entries.description: A listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new register of innovative drugs has been published under sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must monitor this register to ensure their product listings are current and compliant.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.description: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.summary: The EMA issued procedural pre‑authorisation advice for companies using the centralised procedure.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams applying for centralised approvals should read and incorporate the updated guidance to ensure compliance with the EMA’s current expectations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Drug Product Database data extract [2026-10-05]
entries.description: The Drug Product Database (DPD) extract files contain complete product information for all approved, marketed and cancelled products, for human, veterinary, disinfectant and radiopharmaceutical use.
entries.summary: The Drug Product Database has released a new data extract containing comprehensive product information for all approved, marketed, and cancelled products across human, veterinary, disinfectant, and radiopharmaceutical categories.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams should review the updated extract to ensure their product records reflect the latest database content and maintain compliance with reporting requirements.

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling these products must review and ensure their documentation reflects the updated safety information.

entries.title: Advice on ‘end-of-year’ submission dates for type I variations in 2026

entries.summary: Regulators advise type I variation submitters to plan end‑of‑year submission dates for 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: Marketing authorisation holders aiming for 2026 outcomes must time their type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super‑groupings submissions accordingly.

entries.title: EMA Management Board: highlights of September 2026 meeting

entries.summary: EMA presented its first-half 2026 operational results to the Management Board.
entries.why_it_matters: The report provides an overview of EMA activities; RA teams can use this information for internal performance tracking but no immediate compliance actions are required.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Global regulators call for advancing alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle
entries.description: EMA has endorsed a joint statement from the International Coalition of Medicines Regulatory Authorities (ICMRA) calling on medicine developers, manufacturers, regulators and…
entries.summary: Regulators have endorsed a statement urging developers, manufacturers, regulators and others to advance alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should monitor this shift and anticipate potential future policy changes requiring non‑animal testing methods in drug development.

entries.summary: No regulatory change was announced in the speech.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory Affairs teams can simply continue with current processes as no new requirements or deadlines are introduced.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Women are missing from medicines development: EMA’s roadmap for change

But the momentum to improve support for women’s health has never been stronger.…,         Meaningful change starts with dialogue and with a shared understanding of the challenges we face. We end this workshop with a clear path to action”, “National regulatory…,   The multistakeholder workshop, broadcast live, brought together over 100 leading voices on women’s health at EU and international level, from regulators to patients, healthcare…
entries.summary: EMA will develop a regulatory roadmap by the end of 2026 to integrate women’s health considerations into medicines development and regulation.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must plan to include women-specific data in product development and regulatory submissions to comply with the upcoming roadmap.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Updated Register of Certificates of Supplementary Protection and Applications
entries.description: Listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section 120(1) of the Certificate of Supplementary Protection Regulations.
entries.summary: The register of Supplementary Protection Certificates and applications has been updated.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams need to review the updated list to ensure they are aware of any new or altered certificates that could affect product exclusivity timelines.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.description: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.summary: Member states have designated contact points for reviewing the national implementation of QR codes on veterinary medicinal products authorised under CP, MRP, DCP and national procedures.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must use these contact points to ensure compliance with QR code implementation for veterinary products authorised through any of these procedures.

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must be aware of the new coordination process so they can plan and support CHMP‑requested inspections accordingly.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Monthly update to the generic submissions under review list
entries.description: This is a list of certain generic drug submissions currently under review. The Generic Submissions Under Review list includes the medicinal ingredient(s) and therapeutic area. Downloadable Excel files are included.
entries.summary: A list of generic drug submissions currently under review has been updated.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must monitor the updated list to stay informed about which generic submissions are in review and adjust their tracking accordingly.

entries.title: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin

entries.summary: Certain substances are exempt from Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009 concerning veterinary medicinal product residues in animal foodstuffs.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams in veterinary medicine must identify which substances fall outside the regulation to adjust residue monitoring and compliance procedures.

entries.label: MHRA
entries.title: Unlock the MHRA Regulatory Advice Service for Medical Devices

entries.summary: MHRA launched a new Regulatory Advice Service for medical devices in December 2025, allowing developers to consult directly with regulators.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams should be aware that they can now schedule direct meetings with MHRA to clarify device requirements and expedite compliance.

entries.title: Pharmacovigilance-related regulatory recommendations for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products during 2026
